hero.headline: A new dental CAD for the practice and the lab.
hero.subhead: DentalCraft is an application for digital dentistry that you install on your practice or lab computer. It starts with clear aligner planning; more areas of work are planned for later.
hero.microcopy: Early stage. Linux and Windows first. Made in Italy.

presentation.label: Presentation
presentation.headline: What DentalCraft is, and where it stands
presentation.body.1: DentalCraft is a dental CAD. It grows out of an orthodontic aligner planning tool that its author built earlier. It takes up that work and turns it into a dedicated, faster, standalone application, organised like the professional dental CAD suites: a common base and, on top of it, one area for each type of work.
presentation.body.2: The project is at an early stage. The alpha already covers the path from scan import to a first plan: find and separate the teeth, build 3D teeth, analyse the case, register the bite, set a final position, plan the aligners and prepare files for printing. Planning and production are still being validated against the earlier tool: do not rely on their results.

vision.label: Vision
vision.banner: What follows is intent, not a description of finished features.
vision.headline: Why a new dental CAD
vision.body: Digital planning means long hours on heavy scans and 3D models. We think the tool should stay fast, stay on your computer and stay under the clinician's control. DentalCraft is being built around those ideas.
vision.p1.title: Smooth even with heavy scans.
vision.p1.body: The aim: work on the 3D model without freezes, even with large scans.
vision.p2.title: Not tied to a connection.
vision.p2.body: Cases stay on your computer. You should not need the internet to work.
vision.p3.title: One file for each case.
vision.p3.body: The whole case in a single open, documented file, with an integrity check.
vision.p4.title: Pseudonymised patient data.
vision.p4.body: Case files are designed to carry no patient names.
vision.p5.title: In English and Italian.
vision.p6.title: Linux and Windows first.
vision.p7.title: Built with a regulatory mindset.
vision.p7.body: Requirements, risk management and traceability are carried over from day one.
vision.p8.title: Independent and made in Italy.
vision.microcopy: These are design intentions. They describe where we are heading.

aligners.label: Aligners
aligners.headline: From scan to aligner, in one workspace
aligners.body: The Aligners area follows the clinical path from intraoral scan to files for printing. The stages below are grouped like the application menu, and each one says what the alpha already does.
aligners.banner: Status of each stage in the alpha. Planning, production and export are still in development: their results are not validated and must not be used for patients.
aligners.legend.exists: Works in the alpha. Early version, not validated for clinical use.
aligners.legend.inprogress: Partly there. Being worked on or validated.
aligners.s1.stages: Start a case from the New project screen with imported scans (STL, OBJ, PLY), with a scan made by a 3D scanner, or with no scans at all, and add them later in the case, by import or by scanner. An open scan is closed automatically into a clean solid: a flat base under its border, holes inside it filled in place, and a warning that stays on screen if it cannot be closed completely. Remove a scan or an imported model with the bin in the list, the Selected component panel or the Delete key, with a confirmation; Ctrl+Z brings it back. Choose the arch by hand and flip the occlusal side. Scanning inside the app, with or without a turntable, is an early alpha: the automatic turntable scan builds a 0.1 mm surface from all the views, cleans it and closes its holes by itself.
aligners.s2.micro: Get the scans ready for planning.
aligners.s2.stages: Find the teeth and number them (FDI), with an automatic check against teeth found behind the last molars and against neighbours merged into one. The arch ends at the last real molar even when the model base behind it is as high as the tooth, and the check does not join two real teeth whose contact is shallow. A wisdom tooth on one side does not add a phantom tooth on the other, and baby-tooth numbers are refused with a message (they are not supported yet). What the numbering leaves in doubt (the end of the arch left out, a stretch with no crown counted as a space, such as the empty ridge of a missing tooth, or a low stretch left as found) is shown as soon as the step ends, and again when you reopen the project. Marks you can add, delete or renumber by hand, and missing teeth. Separate teeth and gum, with a brush and border cleaning for corrections; while the tooth brush is open, tooth colours and numbers are turned on, and they go back as they were when you leave it. 3D teeth, each a closed solid without holes (tiny tunnels from the scan surface are closed; if a tooth cannot be made, the step says which one failed), with a gum that follows them and is closed with a 3 mm base. See a tooth's region and margin line.
aligners.s3.stages: Case analysis: space, crowding, Little irregularity index, Bolton and the complexity of the case. Enter your own measured values and the results follow them.
aligners.s4.micro: Define the target and the steps. In development: do not use the results for patients.
aligners.s4.stages: Final position, with parameters, the arch line drawn by hand, move a tooth and back to the initial position. Aligners: stages, change calendar, slow a tooth, stage slider. The movement limits per aligner are enforced on every path, automation included, and a value outside them is refused with a message. Steadier plans: a tooth is never delayed against a neighbour that never moves, a delay is kept only when it lowers the worst overlap of its pair, a rotation past the tolerance is corrected only by the excess over it, and a few vertices more or less in the segmentation change the plan less. Collisions the automatic plan cannot solve are listed one by one, in the Aligners panel and in the export report. Clinical review with attachments and interproximal reduction (IPR) marks.
aligners.s5.stages: Bite report, bite scans, registration on the bite scan or with three points picked by hand, bite correction and a contact map. Registration accepts partial or low-quality bite scans: a good front part is enough, and an uncertain result is marked ‘to review’ instead of refused. The bite scan only sets the occlusion of the arches and is not shown in the 3D view. A project with a single arch has no bite: nothing is estimated, the Bite step shows ‘does not apply’, the production settings for the bite with the aligners and the bite ramps say the same, and the aligners are made from that arch alone.
aligners.s6.micro: Prepare the shell and print it. In development.
aligners.s6.stages: Production settings (thickness, clearance, quality), where the aligner ends, trim line with contact bridges, holes and checks, a bar over each missing tooth that keeps the aligner in one piece, clean ends behind the last molars, identification stamps, bite with aligners. The edge of the aligner stays clear of the papillae between the teeth, going round them in a rounded notch, and keeps a small space over the gum it covers; with Advanced options and parameters on, both values can be adjusted, and the fit on the teeth is unchanged. A case where the trim edge could leave a small hole through the wall near the back teeth is fixed. The aligner can be previewed in the 3D view, only when you ask: it is drawn over the scan and over the study model, and follows the timeline. High-quality files are still slow to produce. Print: the aligners are printed directly on the Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K. Each one is turned so that the side that fits the teeth faces away from the plate, gets supports on its outer side only and stands on a U-shaped raft; more positions are tried automatically so that every part can rest on a support; the parts are arranged on the plate and sliced into GOO files with the DENTAL 45 machine parameters. Open or inverted parts, and shells with a hole through the wall, are refused before slicing, the print check agrees with the export check on what counts as a closed solid, and old plate files are not left beside the new ones. A Print window saves the files to a folder or a USB stick (printing over the network is not available yet) and keeps track of which aligners are printed and which are missing. The printer profile's size and left/right orientation are not yet checked against the printer: print a test piece first. Not yet checked on real prints: do not rely on it for patients.
aligners.s7.micro: Compare plan and progress. Early version.
aligners.s7.stages: Control visit: compare a new scan with the plan, and re-plan from a delivered aligner. Tooth-by-tooth tracking is not there yet.
aligners.s8.stages: Export for printing: STL files for each stage (aligners and models), change calendar, report and patient programme. Every passive aligner is engraved with its own number, a P mark and its own date. The export ends in error, naming the files and saying where a hole is, when a file fails the print check. Study models and the export show as done in the step list once they have run. Study models, also shown in the 3D view: each is a clean solid, built from any scan, that keeps the scanned anatomy as it is, undercuts included; two arches that are not in occlusion each get their own base; a study model that is not one clean solid gets a warning and is counted in the report.

new.title: What's new in version {version}
new.note: Planning, production, export and printing are still in development, and 3D scanning is an early alpha. Printing is a preview, in alpha, and has not been checked on real prints yet. Not a medical device. Not for clinical use.
new.1: Saving is safer. DentalCraft never writes a project in a state that cannot be reopened: if something is wrong, the save stops and the previous file stays as it was. A problem with the backup copy is now shown as a warning and no longer blocks saving. A damaged or tampered project file is refused cleanly when you open it, and a project whose step history is empty opens normally instead of being treated as unreadable. A command that changes nothing no longer triggers a save, and the messages about saving and opening projects are now also in Italian.
new.2: More reliable tooth finding. The arch now ends at the last real molar, even when the model base behind it is as high as the tooth, and the automatic check no longer joins two real teeth whose contact is shallow. A wisdom tooth on one side no longer adds a phantom tooth on the other. Baby-tooth numbers are refused with a clear message, because they are not supported yet. A rebuilt tooth is always a solid without holes: tiny tunnels that came from the scan surface are closed, and if a tooth cannot be made, the step tells you which one failed.
new.3: Doubts in tooth finding are shown. As soon as Find the teeth ends, DentalCraft says what the numbering left in doubt: the end of the arch left out, a stretch with no crown counted as a space (such as the empty ridge of a missing tooth), or a low stretch left as found. The notices stay on screen, and they come back when you reopen the project, until you change the marks.
new.4: Scans are closed into a clean solid when you import them. A flat base is put under the border of an open scan, small holes inside the scan are filled in place instead of becoming chimneys down to the base, and faces folded back over the scan are taken out. If a scan still cannot be closed completely, DentalCraft warns you, and the warning stays on screen.
new.5: Study models are clean solids, whatever the scan. They now keep the scanned anatomy as it is, undercuts included, instead of filling everything the crowns hide from above. Two arches that are not in occlusion each get their own base. If a study model is not one clean solid, DentalCraft warns you and the report counts it. The aligner you show stays beside the study model.
new.6: One arch only. When a project has a single arch there is no bite: nothing is estimated, the Bite step shows ‘does not apply’, and the aligners are made from that arch alone. The production settings for the bite with the aligners and the bite ramps say ‘does not apply’ too, and no ‘Bite estimated’ warning appears. The step list is also more accurate: Study models and the export show as done after they have run.
new.7: The four view switches, tooth colours, tooth marks, tooth numbers and the contact map, are always in the toolbar and off by default: in a new project, in an opened one and when the application starts. While the tooth brush is open, tooth colours and numbers are turned on; when you leave it, each goes back as it was.
new.8: The movement limits per aligner are now enforced on every path, automation included. A value outside the limits is refused with a message.
new.9: Steadier automatic planning. A tooth is never delayed against a neighbour that never moves, because that only moves the same contact to a later aligner. A delay is kept only when it lowers the worst overlap of that pair over the whole plan. A rotation past the tolerance is corrected only by the excess over it, and not at all under half a degree. The arch line that decides where the incisors go takes its scale once, from the canines and premolars, and the axis of the last molars holds when a few vertices change. Collisions are checked on every crown point, not on a sample. Together, a few vertices more or less in the segmentation now change the plan less.
new.10: Collisions the automatic plan cannot solve are listed one by one: the aligner, the two teeth, how deep they go and how far over the allowance. The list is in the Aligners panel, also when you reopen the project, and in the export report, in English and Italian.
new.11: A final position that really corrects the arch. The automatic final position now aligns every tooth, premolars and molars included: the teeth behind a space move forward to close it, the midline stays where it is and the last molars never move backwards. No enamel reduction is planned on a contact that is already open, and none to turn a premolar or a molar straight: their rotation is corrected only as far as the arch has room. With Advanced options and parameters on, you can allow the last molars to move back by up to 0.5 mm. Projects saved with the old defaults take the new ones when opened.
new.12: Aligner fit on the gum. The aligner keeps a small space over the gum it covers, and its edge stays at least 1 mm above the tip of every papilla and 2 mm from the gum line of every tooth. The fit on the teeth is unchanged.
new.13: A straight aligner between the teeth. The edge of the aligner is now straight, at the height of the widest part of each crown, and the aligner goes straight from one tooth to the next: it no longer enters the spaces between the teeth, above or below the contact, where it was fragile and in the way. Projects saved with this version open in older versions with the aligner settings read-only.
new.14: The aligner you ask to see in the 3D view is now drawn also over the scan and over the study model, and it follows the timeline.
new.15: Aligner shells and export: a case where the trim edge could leave a small hole through the wall near the back teeth is fixed, and the export check now says where a hole is. Every passive aligner is engraved with its own number, a P mark and its own date.
new.16: Print preparation: open or inverted parts, and shells with a hole through the wall, are refused before slicing. The print check agrees with the export check on what counts as a closed solid, and the parts are read exactly as saved. More positions are tried automatically so that every part can rest on a support; when no position works, the message says the shell itself needs correcting. Old plate files are no longer left beside the new ones. A warning now says that the printer profile's size and left/right orientation are not yet checked against the printer, so print a test piece first. Printing is still a preview in alpha, not yet checked on real prints.
new.17: The step list follows the case. A step shows as done only while the case holds its result, Undo and Redo bring the steps back as they were, and an export or a run of everything stays done until a setting or a step run again makes it out of date.
new.18: Sign-in and updates: a wrong computer clock no longer signs you out, and DentalCraft shows a message about the clock instead. The installer is checked again right before it runs.
new.19: Diagnostics, only if you opt in: folder names and device serial numbers are removed more thoroughly from what is sent, and only you can give the consent, in the application.
new.20: Automation: the local control port of the running application, used by dentalcraft-cli and its MCP server, now requires a secret created at each launch. The command-line tool finds it by itself.
new15.1: Bite registration now works with partial or low-quality bite scans. A good front part of the scan is enough: when the result is uncertain, DentalCraft registers the bite and marks it ‘to review’ instead of refusing it. It still refuses a bite scan whose position cannot be worked out, or that does not fit (a mirrored one, for example).
new15.2: The bite scan is used only to put the upper and lower arches in occlusion, and it is no longer shown in the 3D view. It appears only while you pick the three points by hand.
new15.3: Scans and imported models can be removed from the case. Use the bin on a row of the scan list or of the bite list, the Remove the scan button in the Selected component panel, or the Delete or Backspace key on a selected scan. DentalCraft asks you to confirm, clears what was computed from that scan, and Ctrl+Z brings it all back.
new15.4: 3D teeth always produces closed models: each tooth is a closed solid, and the gum is closed with a 3 mm base.
new15.5: More reliable automatic tooth numbering. A check now corrects teeth wrongly found behind the last molars and neighbouring teeth wrongly merged into one.
new14.1: The print window now takes the side that fits the teeth from the stage model saved with the export, so that side is known and not guessed from the shape of the aligner.
new14.2: When the stage model is not available and DentalCraft has to guess the fitting side from the shape, the print window warns you: check the orientation before you print. Printing is still a preview in alpha, not yet checked on real prints.
new13.1: A Settings window, opened from the menu at the top right. It gathers the general options, the workspace, updates and privacy in one place.
new13.2: A simple interface by default. With Advanced options and parameters off, which is the default, the side panels show only the automatic steps and the most useful corrections, and the menu marks the Next step to take. Turn the option on to see every parameter and technical value.
new13.3: Print the aligners directly. A new Print window prepares the aligners for the Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K: each one is turned automatically so that the side that fits the teeth faces away from the plate, supports are added on the outer side only, and each part stands on a U-shaped raft.
new13.4: The parts are arranged on the plate and sliced into GOO files with the printer's DENTAL 45 machine parameters. You save the files to a folder or a USB stick and print from the printer. Printing over the network is not available yet.
new13.5: DentalCraft keeps track of each aligner: printed, or still missing. The record is saved with the case. Printing is a preview in alpha: it has not been checked on real prints yet, so the printed aligners are not validated.
new13.6: The code is public on GitHub (source-available, under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0) and the documentation is online at https://dnviti.github.io/dentalcraft-docs/. Both are linked from the About page and from the footer.

technology.label: In practice
technology.headline: Your work, your data
technology.body: Choices made for speed, control and traceability of the work.
technology.i1.title: An application on your computer.
technology.i1.body: You install and use it on the practice or lab computer, not through a browser. Installers for Linux and Windows check for updates and ask before installing them.
technology.i2.title: A smooth 3D view.
technology.i2.body: Click any tooth, gum or scan to select it and see it outlined, then move, rotate or scale it in the view. Designed to stay smooth even with detailed scans: the frame rate is capped at 60 per second with vsync, and the menu and details panels can be resized.
technology.i3.title: One file for each case.
technology.i3.body: An open, documented file with an integrity check. It is saved automatically a moment after each change, and whenever you save. A project is never written in a state that cannot be reopened: if something is wrong, the save stops and the previous file stays.
technology.i4.title: Privacy by design.
technology.i4.body: Patient data is pseudonymised: no names in case files. Anonymous diagnostics are sent only if you opt in.
technology.i5.title: Cases stay with you.
technology.i5.body: You work on cases saved on your computer. An account is planned for licences and support only.
technology.i6.title: Two languages.
technology.i7.title: Driven by scripts and AI agents.
technology.i7.body: Every action is also a command of dentalcraft-cli and its MCP server, so scripts and AI agents can run the same steps. The local control port of the running application needs a secret created at each launch.
technology.i8.title: Nothing silently out of date.
technology.i8.body: When you change a step, the later results that depend on it are listed as out of date.
technology.microcopy: Details will be published once the file format is final.
regulatory.label: Regulatory
regulatory.headline: Honest about where we are
regulatory.callout: In development. Not a medical device. Not for clinical use.
regulatory.body.1: DentalCraft is not a medical device and is not certified. It must not be used for clinical purposes.
regulatory.body.2: The project is being built with a regulatory mindset: requirements, risk management and traceability are taken over from the earlier work. The intention is to pursue the appropriate medical-device conformity path when the software is ready for it. That is an intention, not a status.
faq.label: FAQ
faq.headline: Questions, answered plainly
faq.a1: An alpha version for Linux and Windows can be downloaded from the home page, free of charge, for non-clinical use (evaluation, training, research and design trials). It is in early development: it is not a medical device and not for clinical use. It already lets you import scans, find and separate the teeth, build 3D teeth, analyse the case, register the bite, set a final position, plan the aligners and prepare files for printing. Planning and production are still in development.
faq.q2: Is it certified? Is it a medical device?
faq.a2: No. DentalCraft is not a medical device and holds no certification. It is not for clinical use. We are building with a regulatory mindset and intend to pursue the appropriate conformity path in the future.
faq.q3: Which computers will it run on?
faq.a3: Linux and Windows first. macOS later.
faq.a4: Yes. The alpha can be downloaded and used free of charge for non-commercial purposes, under the PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 licence (source-available). Commercial use needs a licence from the author. It is not for clinical use. See the licence page for the terms.
faq.a5: Cases are designed to stay on your computer. Case files are pseudonymised and carry no patient names. Scans, projects and patient data are never sent to us. An account is planned only for licences and support.
faq.a6: Yes. An alpha version for Linux and Windows can be downloaded from the home page, free of charge, for non-clinical use: evaluation, training, research and design trials. It is provided as is. It is not a medical device and not for clinical use.
faq.a7: The first area is Aligners, for clear aligner planning. The home page lists every stage with its status. From scan import to the bite it works in the alpha; the final position, the aligners, the clinical review, production and export are still in development, and their results are not validated: do not use them for patients.
faq.a8: You can import scans in STL, OBJ and PLY; open scans are closed automatically with a base. You can also scan with a supported 3D scanner (early alpha), from the New project screen or later in the case, and add the result to the project. Export for printing writes STL files for each stage, with a change calendar and a report, and it ends in error if a file fails the print check: that function is still being completed. Each case is saved in a single open file, automatically a moment after each change and whenever you save.
faq.q9: Can I use it from scripts or with an AI agent?
faq.a9: Yes. Every action in the application, scanning and the turntable included, is also a command of the dentalcraft-cli tool, which comes with the standalone downloads and the installers, and of its MCP server, so a script or an AI agent can run the same steps.
faq.a10: The Flatpak, Fedora and Debian/Ubuntu versions update with your system. All the others check this site when DentalCraft starts, ask before updating and verify the signature of the update before installing it.
faq.q11: Can I scan with a 3D scanner inside DentalCraft?
faq.a11: Yes, as an early alpha. On the New project screen, a Scan button next to Browse files… opens a scan window, and the same window opens from Scan import in the case: connect a scanner, start, pause and stop the live capture, clean up the point cloud, create the surface and add it to the project as upper arch, lower arch or bite. With the turntable, an automatic scan stops the table at each position, captures it standing still and rebuilds the surface from all the views at 0.1 mm, then cleans it, closes its holes and simplifies it; the views of a piece that moved are left out, so fix the model firmly to the platter. The window is shared by the whole application, so any area of work can offer it. It works with the Revopoint MINI 2 over USB on Linux and, new in version 0.2.0-alpha.9, on Windows (still alpha, tested so far in a Windows virtual machine), with no vendor SDK, using the calibration stored in the scanner (read automatically) or, failing that, an approximate one, unless you supply a calibration file. The Revopoint 3D Camera SDK can be used as an optional backend: you supply it, with Revopoint's own authorisation, and it is not bundled. A built-in simulated scanner lets you try the workflow without hardware. On Windows the scanner is read through the system's Media Foundation video capture, and the fill light, the fast exposure and reading the stored calibration work as on Linux. The Revopoint Dual-axis Turntable works over Bluetooth LE (tested on Linux and Windows) and reconnects by itself if the link drops during a scan; if the scanner or the table moved since the turntable calibration, the automatic scan stops after its first views and asks you to calibrate again. Not a medical device: do not use scans made this way for clinical decisions.
faq.q12: Can I start a project without scans?
faq.a12: Yes. On the New project screen scans are optional: import files, scan with a supported 3D scanner (early alpha), or create the project empty. In the project you can add the upper arch, lower arch and bite later, by import or with the scanner. Not a medical device: do not use it for clinical decisions.
faq.q13: Does DentalCraft send any data to you?
faq.a13: Only if you agree. At first start the application asks whether it may send anonymous diagnostic data (crash reports, error messages, the version, system and graphics card, and recent log lines with folder names and device serial numbers removed) to help fix bugs. The box is unticked by default and you can change it at any time in the account menu. Scans, projects, patient data and account data are never sent. See the privacy note for the full list.
faq.q14: What are Settings and the simple interface?
faq.a14: Settings opens from the menu at the top right and gathers the general options, the workspace, updates and privacy. Its option Advanced options and parameters is off by default: the side panels then show only the automatic steps and the most useful corrections, and the menu marks the Next step to take. Turn it on to see every parameter and technical value.
faq.q15: Can I print the aligners with DentalCraft?
faq.a15: Yes, directly, on the Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K. The Print window turns each aligner so that the side that fits the teeth faces away from the plate, adds supports on the outer side only and a U-shaped raft, arranges the parts on the plate and slices them into GOO files with the DENTAL 45 machine parameters. You save the files to a folder or a USB stick and print from the printer; printing over the network is planned, not available yet. DentalCraft also keeps track of which aligners are printed and which are missing. It has not been checked on real prints yet, so do not use the printed aligners on patients. Not a medical device.
faq.q16: Where are the source code and the documentation?
faq.a16: The source code is public on GitHub, under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 (source-available, not open source). The documentation is at https://dnviti.github.io/dentalcraft-docs/.

privacy.label: Privacy
privacy.headline: No tracking on the site; app diagnostics only if you agree
privacy.body.1: This website sets no cookies, runs no analytics or tracking scripts, loads nothing from third parties and has no forms. We do not collect personal data through it. Your language choice is kept only in your own browser, so that the site can open in your language next time.
privacy.body.2: Like any website, this one may keep standard access logs (IP address, time, page requested) for security and troubleshooting. If you write to hello@dentalcraft.app, we use your message only to reply.
privacy.app.title: The application: anonymous diagnostics, only if you opt in
privacy.app.1: The DentalCraft application can send anonymous diagnostic data to the developer, to find and fix bugs. It is off until you agree: at first start a window asks you, with the checkbox unticked, and you can change your choice at any time in the account menu. Only you can give the consent, in the application. If you do not agree, nothing is collected or sent.
privacy.app.2: What is sent: the application version and how it was installed; your operating system and language; the graphics card and its driver, the amount of memory and the number of processors; crash reports with their backtrace; error and warning codes and messages; the latest log lines before a problem, with folder names and device serial numbers removed; one record each time the application starts; and a random installation ID, generated on your computer and not linked to your account.
privacy.app.3: What is never sent: scans, projects and case files, patient data, case aliases or codes, file names, and account data (name, email, sign-in tokens). The server does not store your IP address with this data.
privacy.app.4: Where it goes and for how long: only to DentalCraft's own server (auth.dentalcraft.app), never to a third party. It is kept for 90 days, then deleted, and it is used only to find and fix bugs. If you turn the option off, the data not yet sent and the installation ID are deleted from your computer. Questions: hello@dentalcraft.app.
